REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 10, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.

Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
MARCH 10, 2022, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational update on the Tuesday, April 12, 2022 Cerritos General Municipal Election was
  given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Elections Official. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Rocky Pavone spoke regarding his campaign for election to the Cerritos City Council.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding his campaign for election to the Cerritos City Council,
  encouraged residents to vote early, requested teleconference public meeting access, and
  spoke regarding the fiber optic feasibility study, crime in Cerritos, and the Cerritos Electric
  Utility program.

  Patricia Murray spoke regarding her campaign for election to the Cerritos City Council and
  in support of district-based elections.

  Case van der Linden expressed concerns regarding the care and maintenance of City trees.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 10, 2022, 7:00 p.m.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, February 24, 2022, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the Thursday,
  February 24, 2022, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 10, 2022 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  March 10, 2022  $ 4,424,360.46 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2022
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2022
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 10, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING AND IMPLEMENTING TELECONFRENCE
  ACCESSIBLITY FOR CONDUCTION PUBLIC MEETNGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361
  (STATS. 2021, CH. 165) (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2022-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF  CERRITOS,  CALIFORNIA,  AUTHORIZING  AND  IMPLEMENTING
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (STATS. 2021, CH. 165) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Rosewood Park Playground
  Improvements, Project No. 22105, Bid No. 1450-22 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Deputy Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to continue this item to the 7:00
  p.m., Thursday, April 14, 2022 City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting and direct
  staff to include in their report other options that may be available for use of these CDBG
  funds (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and approval of a Power Sales Agreement with Southern California Public Power
  Authority for the purchase of solar power and battery storage through the Daggett Solar
  Power 2 Project (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Utilities Administrator. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 10, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  Sam Desai inquired regarding the beneficiaries as a result of this project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Find that approval of the proposed action is exempt from California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) review, because it is an administrative and fiscal activity that will
  not result in direct or indirect physical changes in the environment, and therefore does
  not constitute a “project” as defined by CEQA Guidelines section 15378; with regard to
  the underlying project and pursuant to the Power Purchase Agreement between SCPPA
  and Daggett Solar Power 2 LLC, the lead agencies have obtained all CEQA
  determinations required for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the
  facility; and

  2.  Direct staff to reduce the output of the Magnolia Power Project to accommodate the
  energy procured from the Daggett Solar Power 2 Project; and

  3.  Approve and authorize the City Manager to enter into the Power Sales Agreement with
  SCPPA, in substantially the same form as submitted, for the purchase of 5 megawatts
  of solar power and 3 megawatts of battery storage with the associated green
  attributes though the Daggett Solar 2 Project for a projected annual cost of $645,000
  over a 20-year term (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to add an agenda item to the March
  24, 2022 agenda for review and consideration of letters of support or opposition, as
  applicable, related to the following pending legislation items: AB 1599, AB 1603, and AB
  1597.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  An informational report on the construction of site and building improvements at the City-
  owned property located at 12616 183rd Street, Project No. 18206, was given by Dario
  Simoes, Deputy Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 10, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 5

11.  Reports (continued)

11A.  (continued)

  An informational report on the City’s receipt of a federal transit administration Buses and
  Bus Facility Grant Award was given by Kristin Aguila, Director of Community Development.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Solanki, Mayor Pro Tem Vo.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:48 p.m. in memory of Beverly Porter.

  /s/ Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

 /s/ Grace Hu  _
